contract: X.Org twm 1.0.13.1 f.warptoscreen selection/history and the wtwm Wayland output translation

manual.target.text: This function warps the pointer to the screen specified by the

manual.next.text: \fB"1"\fP), the word \fB"next"\fP (indicating the current screen plus 1,

manual.back.text: the word \fB"back"\fP (indicating the current screen minus 1, skipping over

warp.warning.text: twmWarning("unable to warp to unmanaged screen %d", n);

history.declaration.text: int PreviousScreen;             /* last screen that we were on */

runtime.warp-entry.text: static void warp_to_screen(struct server *server, const char *argument) {

observed: The parser already normalizes and admits next, prev, back, and decimal f.warptoscreen arguments.
The portable target helper already models named cycling and strict numeric rejection.
The compositor already creates a canonical enabled-output snapshot, locates the pointer by half-open output containment, warps it, and reprocesses pointer focus.
This contract fixes the complete history and target-clamping semantics that the implementation slice and live tests must prove.

argument_language.rule: The grammar lowercases the argument and accepts next, prev, back, or an ASCII-digit string; named actions are therefore case-insensitive. The empty string also passes the frozen digit loop and reaches atoi as zero.

target_selection.numeric: A numeric argument is converted with atoi and requested directly; WarpToScreen wraps a negative value once to NumScreens-1 and a value at least NumScreens once to zero.
target_selection.next: next starts at Scr->screen + 1, walks in increasing X-screen-number order, wraps, and skips unmanaged ScreenList entries until a managed screen is found.
target_selection.prev: prev starts at Scr->screen - 1, walks in decreasing X-screen-number order, wraps, and skips unmanaged ScreenList entries until a managed screen is found.
target_selection.back: back directly requests PreviousScreen without walking; an unmanaged target warns, rings the bell, and returns.
target_selection.manual_code_discrepancy: The manual says back means current-minus-one and prev means last-visited. The dispatch source does the opposite: prev decrements and back uses PreviousScreen. Source is authoritative for this contract.

history.initial: PreviousScreen is initialized to DefaultScreen at process startup.
history.successful_different_target: Immediately before a warp to a different managed screen, PreviousScreen becomes the source Scr->screen. Repeated back operations therefore toggle between the last two successfully visited screens.
history.same_target: A target equal to Scr->screen returns before the history assignment, pointer query, or warp; history is unchanged.
history.no_target: An unmanaged direct numeric/back target returns after warning and bell; history is unchanged.
history.interactive_placement: During the first interactive AddWindow placement query, if the pointer root differs from Scr->Root and maps to an X screen, PreviousScreen is set to that pointer-root screen before the later root warp.
history.restart: f.restart replaces the process with execvp; successful restart reconstructs PreviousScreen from DefaultScreen, while failed exec leaves the running process and its history intact.

pointer_mapping.rule: After selecting a different managed screen, twm queries pointer coordinates relative to the source root and supplies the same x and y as destination-root coordinates; it does not scale them by source or target dimensions.
pointer_mapping.edge_behavior: X server pointer constraints determine the observable edge result when unchanged coordinates lie outside the target root.

wayland_translation.classification: behaviorally-equivalent output translation with the previously documented strict numeric safety difference

active_domain.outputs: Operate only on enabled compositor-managed Wayland outputs in one canonical output-order snapshot. Dense indices are zero-based within that snapshot.
active_domain.current: The current output is the unique canonical-first output whose logical layout box contains the pointer under half-open bounds. A pointer in a layout gap or outside every enabled output has no current output.
active_domain.identity_index: next, prev, and numeric targets resolve canonical indices ordered by immutable output identities in the operation snapshot. Previous history denotes the prior visited output within a fixed canonical topology; back resolves that abstract reference in the same snapshot. Whether the stored representation is an index or identity is deliberately not observable in this slice.
active_domain.single_snapshot: Current selection, named/numeric target resolution, history lookup, source geometry, and target geometry use the same snapshot so one action cannot mix canonical index generations.

target_selection.numeric: Preserve the screen-output contract: accept only a complete unsigned ASCII decimal value that fits int and is less than the snapshot count; invalid, signed, malformed, overflow, and out-of-range forms resolve to no target.
target_selection.next: Select (current + 1) modulo the enabled-output count in canonical identity order.
target_selection.prev: Select (current + count - 1) modulo the enabled-output count in canonical identity order. This follows source, not the swapped manual prose.
target_selection.back: If the previous-output reference resolves in the snapshot, select it; if history is unset or missing, resolve to no target. A successful back replaces history with the source output reference, so repeated back toggles.
target_selection.no_skip_holes: The enabled-output snapshot is dense, so named traversal has no unmanaged holes to skip; disabled outputs are absent rather than skipped entries.

history.startup: Start with no previous-output reference, including startup with zero outputs. Do not synthesize output zero as history merely because an output later appears.
history.successful_different_target: After resolving a present target different from current and completing the pointer warp, record the source output as previous.
history.same_target: A numeric, next, prev, or back action resolving to current is a no-op and does not change history.
history.no_target: Zero outputs, no current output, a gap/outside pointer, invalid numeric input, unset/missing back history, snapshot/allocation failure, or an absent source/target causes no pointer or history mutation.
history.one_output: With one enabled output, next and prev wrap to current, numeric zero names current, and back is unset or current; all are no-ops and leave history unchanged.
history.reload: Configuration reload is not a screen visit. A valid atomic reload preserves previous-output history; an invalid replacement preserves the active configuration and history.
history.restart: The in-place f.restart/f.twmrc alias models reference process restart for ephemeral navigation state: after a successful replacement it clears previous-output history; a rejected replacement leaves history unchanged.
history.client_events: Native map, Xwayland map, focus, activation, placement, and ordinary pointer motion do not write screen history. The reference AddWindow cross-root write has no Wayland analogue because outputs are not independent X roots and output-aware placement does not warp the seat between roots.

pointer_mapping.relative_rule: Compute source-relative offsets dx = pointer_x - source.x and dy = pointer_y - source.y, then target coordinates target.x + clamp(dx, 0, target.width - 1) and target.y + clamp(dy, 0, target.height - 1). Do not scale proportional positions.
pointer_mapping.target_clamp: Clamp to the selected target's half-open logical box before the cursor warp. Never let a global nearest-layout fallback redirect an oversized relative coordinate into a different output.
pointer_mapping.post_warp: After a successful coordinate change, process cursor motion once so root/client context, focus policy, cursor role, and subsequent bindings observe the destination immediately.

context_invariance.rule: The one seat's pointer location and canonical output snapshot determine current and target. Root, menu, key, title, frame, window, icon, icon-manager, or named-function invocation context does not substitute a focused window's owner output.
context_invariance.protocols: The same action state machine and history apply when the invoking binding was reached through a native Wayland client or a managed Xwayland client; client protocol, app_id, title, WM_NAME, WM_CLASS, stacking, focus, and iconification do not alter output traversal.
context_invariance.gaps: Root bindings do not fire in gaps under the output-placement contract; if another context invokes f.warptoscreen while the pointer has no current output, it is still a no-op.

topology_boundary.fixed_snapshot: This slice defines complete warp behavior against one stable action snapshot and an abstract previous-output reference whose index-or-identity storage representation is not prescribed.
topology_boundary.next_task: The following output-topology task owns transaction timing for add/remove/enable/disable, scale, transform, mode, and layout changes; the history representation plus renumbering, invalidation, or repair when canonical membership/order changes; pointer repair during concurrent topology change; and policy for a removed current/previous output.
topology_boundary.non_claim: Passing fixed-topology numeric/next/prev/back tests does not claim output hotplug, rearrangement, mode/scale safety, disappeared-output restoration, multiple seats, or session-state persistence.

this_slice_requires: source-authoritative numeric, next, prev, and back target semantics
exact successful, same-target, no-target, one-output, reload, and restart history rules
canonical identity-ordered index resolution and previous-output history in one fixed action snapshot
output-relative unscaled pointer mapping clamped to the selected target
native/Xwayland and invocation-context invariant behavior with gap and zero-output safety
explicitly_deferred: output add/remove/enable/disable transaction timing and history repair when an identity disappears
output scale, transform, mode, and layout-change transaction mechanics
safe restoration or relocation of windows after an output disappears
input hotplug and multiple keyboards, pointers, seats, or independent seat focus
session startup, logout, failure recovery, and persistent state-file lifecycle
scope_boundaries.non_claim: This contract completes only steady-state f.warptoscreen selection, pointer mapping, and ephemeral previous-output history. It does not complete the following topology, restoration, input, session, Milestone 8 testing, or exit-criteria checkboxes.

requirements.rule: Treat source as authoritative: next increments, prev decrements, back uses PreviousScreen, and numeric dispatch uses atoi in frozen twm despite contradictory manual prose.
Preserve evidence that only a successful different-screen warp and the special cross-root AddWindow path update PreviousScreen, while same or unmanaged targets do not.
Resolve current, numeric, next, prev, and previous-output back targets from one dense identity-ordered canonical enabled-output snapshot.

Record the source output only after a successful different-output warp; preserve history for same-target/no-target paths and reload, clear it on successful in-place restart, and make repeated back toggle.
Preserve unscaled source-relative pointer coordinates, clamp them to the selected target output, and refresh pointer context once after success.
Zero outputs, gaps/outside, missing history, invalid targets, and one-output same targets cause no pointer or history mutation.
Use one seat pointer state independent of native/Xwayland protocol, focused-client ownership, and action invocation context.
Do not claim add/remove/scale/mode transaction safety, missing-identity history repair, removed-window restoration, multiple seats, or session lifecycle from fixed-topology warp coverage.

verification_scenarios.oracle: Frozen dispatch proves prev decrements and back selects PreviousScreen despite the manual swapping those descriptions.
next/prev walk past unmanaged ScreenList holes, while numeric/back to an unmanaged entry warn and leave history unchanged.
A successful different-screen warp stores the source, same-screen warp does not, and repeated back toggles.
The frozen interactive AddWindow cross-root path is the only evidenced non-warp PreviousScreen write.
next advances through canonical indices and wraps from the last enabled output to index zero.
prev decrements through canonical indices and wraps index zero to the last enabled output.
After two different-output visits, successive back actions alternate exact pointer positions between the last two outputs.
A valid numeric warp to a different output records the source for back; an invalid numeric target changes neither pointer nor history.
Numeric current, one-output next/prev, and back-to-current leave exact pointer coordinates and previous history unchanged.
back before any successful different-output warp is a no-op rather than selecting canonical index zero.
An equal-sized target receives the same output-relative x/y without proportional scaling.
An oversized source-relative coordinate clamps to target width-1/height-1 and cannot land on a neighboring output.
Invocation while the pointer is in a layout gap changes neither coordinates nor history.
Every screen argument is a no-op with zero outputs and does not synthesize history.
Both successful config reload and rejected replacement preserve the established previous-output reference.
Successful in-place f.restart/f.twmrc clears navigation history; rejected replacement preserves it.
Native client/window/menu/root invocation reaches the same pointer-selected canonical traversal and history state.
Managed Xwayland focus, identity, owner output, and invocation context do not alter pointer-selected traversal or history.
Passing warp tests does not claim safe concurrent topology transactions, missing-output repair, restoration, multiple seats, or session persistence.
